message.content:
**When the pain and shortness of breath started**  
The pain began last night, right after the catheter that was draining my urinary pouch stopped working. Within a few hours I started feeling a severe ache in my lower abdomen, and the shortness of breath got worse as the night went on.  

**How I would describe the pain**  
- **Location:** Lower abdomen, around the area of the pouch.  
- **Quality:** It feels like a deep, steady pressure that is very uncomfortable – more “tight” or “cramping” than sharp.  
- **Pattern:** It has been constant since it started and has not gone away.  
- **Radiation:** I haven’t felt it spreading to any other part of my body.  

**What kind of catheter I was using**  
I have an indwelling catheter that sits in my continent MAINZ pouch I (the urinary diversion I had after my radical cystectomy). It’s placed for continuous drainage of the pouch.  

**What happened when the drainage “failed”**  
Last night the catheter stopped draining. I noticed that the amount of urine coming out dropped a lot – almost no urine was coming out at all. It felt like the catheter became blocked or stopped working, so the pouch was no longer emptying. That is when the severe lower‑abdominal pain and the increasing shortness of breath started.
